entries.title: Potts boundary relative entropy has a surface bound (unreviewed draft)
entries.statement: Draft author claim, independent review pending. On the SAME finite variable region, let gamma_f be the integer-q zero-field Potts Gibbs law with unit ferromagnetic internal bonds and gamma_b the law with exterior spins fixed. For beta>=0, q>=2 and m crossing bonds, D(gamma_b||gamma_f)<=beta*m and D(gamma_f||gamma_b)<=beta*m. Every mixture rho of the exterior-boundary laws has D(rho||gamma_f)<=beta*m. For n^d lattice boxes this gives D(rho||gamma_f)/n^d<=2*d*beta/n, at every temperature. It does not give an energy gap. Pinning variable sites in only one law would violate the common-support hypothesis.
assumptions: unit ferromagnetic bonds and zero field
identical variable sites; only exterior spins are pinned

entries.title: Vanishing entropy deficits can certify a pressure jump (unreviewed draft)
entries.statement: Draft author claim, independent review pending. Define P_n(t)=log Z_n^free(t)/|Lambda_n| for growing nearest-neighbor Potts boxes. Assume P_n converges to P on an open interval about beta_*. If two probability-law sequences rho_n^+ and rho_n^- have D(rho_n^sign||gamma_{n,beta_*}^free)/|Lambda_n| tending to zero, and their expected internal agreement counts per vertex tend to e_+>e_-, then P'_+(beta_*)-P'_-(beta_*)>=e_+-e_->0. The proof takes volume limits before the temperature increment tends to zero. Establishing that beta_* equals the order/disorder critical point, and bridging an energy jump to its magnetization definition, are separate obligations.

entries.title: Product Potts trials have an extensive entropy deficit (unreviewed draft)
entries.statement: Draft author claim, independent review pending. On a finite simple graph G=(V,E), let u be uniform independent integer-q spins and gamma_beta its free zero-field unit-bond Potts Gibbs law. For q>=2 and beta>=0, D(u||gamma_beta)>=|E|*c_q(beta), where c_q(beta)=log((exp(beta)+q-1)/q)-beta/q. Equality holds on forests, and the bound is strict when beta>0 and G has a cycle. On Z^d boxes the limiting deficit per vertex is at least d*c_q(beta)>0 for beta>0. For any fixed full-support product law pi, an induced matching gives the alternative positive lower bound 2*(min pi)^4*tanh(beta/2)^2/(3*2^(d-1)) per vertex. Thus neither uniform nor full-support fixed product trials satisfy a vanishing-deficit hypothesis at positive beta.
assumptions: finite simple graph for finite bound
zero field and unit ferromagnetic bonds
growing n^d lattice boxes for limiting statements
full support for the nonuniform product bound

entries.title: C0048 entropy route excludes a mean-field product shortcut (unreviewed draft)
entries.statement: C0048 asks for positive critical spontaneous magnetization for every integer q>=3 and d>=3 in the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Potts model. Current openness is UNKNOWN; no solution is claimed. At beta_MF=(q-1)*log(q-1)/(d*(q-2)), uniform product spins and the ordered product law pi_1=(q-1)/q, pi_i=1/(q*(q-1)) for i>1 have equal limiting scores S(pi)+beta_MF*d*sum(pi_i^2). Both have the SAME positive limiting entropy deficit, at least d*c_q(beta_MF), where c_q(beta)=log((exp(beta)+q-1)/q)-beta/q. Their mean-field score equality is not critical coexistence. The hardest remaining step is constructing correlated critical trial laws with vanishing entropy deficits and a positive limiting agreement-density separation.
assumptions: integer q>=3 and d>=3 for the C0048 target
unit nearest-neighbor interaction; beta is the agreement convention
no assertion that beta_MF equals beta_c
all supporting author proofs are unreviewed

relations.rationale: The route uses surface entropy to obtain zero deficits for actual Gibbs marginals.
The route requires two zero-deficit trial laws with different limiting energies.
The product shortcut is excluded by an explicit positive limiting entropy deficit.
Same exact integer-q nearest-neighbor critical Potts target, verified in the existing live target node; this is only a partial attempt.
